LINK R1 OPPOSITION LANDOWNERS' OBJECTIONS TO AND MOTION TO
STRIKE PORTIONS OF DIRECT TESTIMONY AND EXHIBITS

COMES NOW, Dennis Grafa (“Grafa”), Gary and Katherine Johnson (“Johnson”), Tana
Autrey (“Autrey”), 9-Campbell Ranch, L.P. (“9-Campbell Ranch”), Sharon Holman as Trustee of
the Charles Ray Pfluger Shelter Trust (“Charles Ray Pfluger Trust”), Melissa O’ Harrow and James
Hamilton O’Harrow Family Trust (“O’Harrow”), and Chase B. Akin (“Akin”) (collectively the
“Link RI Opposition Landowners”) and submit these objections and motion to strike portions of
the direct testimony filed by (1) John A. “Matt” Mathews, Jr. on behalf of KLM Griffen Ranch,
L.P. (“Mr. Mathews”) — Item 3876 ; (2) William Reid Pfluger on behalf of the Pfluger Family
Limited Partnership (“Pfluger”) — Item 3881; (3) Carolyn Quillen on behalf of William Quillen,
James Blake Quillen, and Quillen Family Partnership, Ltd. (“Quillen”) — Item 3877; and (4)
Carolyn Quillen (“Quillen”) — Item 3878.

I. BACKGROUND
Under the procedural schedule adopted for this proceeding, May 18, 2026, is the deadline
for Objection to Intervenor Direct Testimony. Accordingly, these objections and motion to strike

are timely filed.

 2 of 10

Il. OBJECTION AND MOTION TO STRIKE PORTIONS OF DIRECT
TESTIMONY AND EXHIBITS 2-33 OF THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
JOHN A. “MATT” MATHEWS, JR. (“MR. MATHEWS”) ON BEHALF OF
KLM GRIFFEN RANCH, L.P. (“KLM”) AND VARIOUS TESTIMONY OF
QUILLEN AND PFLUGER

Link R1 Opposition Landowners objects to various portions of the direct testimony of Mr.
Mathews, Pfluger, and Quillen as improper lay witness testimony since they are not an expert
witness. Additionally, certain testimony and exhibits in Mr. Mathews’ direct testimony contain
hearsay or call for an answer based on hearsay, documents that lack foundation and are not
properly authenticated, lack direct knowledge, and/or call for a legal conclusion. These portions

are detailed in Section III.

A. Lack of Personal Knowledge

Under Tex. R. Evid. 602, a witness may not testify to a matter “unless evidence is
introduced sufficient to support a finding that the witness has personal knowledge of the matter.”
Mr. Mathews offers testimony, including Exhibits 2-33, of which he lacks personal knowledge.
He presented no evidence or testimony to show that he created, or even has personal knowledge
of, the facts, data, and information contained in some testimony and in his attached Exhibits 2-33.

Similarly, Pfluger and Quillen offer some testimony, but they have presented no evidence
or testimony that they have any personal knowledge of the facts they are testifying to. These

specific items are addressed in the charts below.

B. Inappropriate Opinion Testimony - Mr. Mathews is not an Expert

Under Tex. Rules of Evid. 701, a non-expert witness may only provide testimony in the
form of opinion when it is limited to one “rationally based on the witness’s perception.” Link R1
Opposition Landowners do not object to the testimony offered by Mr. Mathews, Pfluger, or
Quillen, about their own land and what they have personal knowledge of; instead, the objections
are to testimony and exhibits that are founded on what others have told them or what they have
read somewhere. When a witness offers an opinion as an expert, it must come from a witness who

is “qualified as an expert by knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education.” Mr. Mathews

 3 of 10

has not been designated as an expert in any field, and no facts or qualifications have been provided
to show that he has any specialized knowledge, training, skill, or experience related to any
particular subject matter. Similarly, neither Quillen nor Pfluger have been offered or shown to be
an expert.

Nothing in Mr. Mathews, Pfluger, or either Quillens’ direct testimony identifies them as
an expert, or that he or she has any specialized training, skill, experience, education, or knowledge
to provide an expert opinion testimony related to 1) archeology, 2) hydrology, or 3) the law.!
Accordingly, in some of the testimony offered by Mr. Mathews, he makes an opinion and
statements about facts and data he has no personal knowledge of, but instead is relying on other
information, data, and statements, his Exhibits 2-33. These exhibits are not admissible for reasons
stated herein. Mr. Mathews is not an expert, and accordingly, he cannot rely on hearsay evidence

as experts can under Tex. R. Evid. 703.

C. Inadmissible Hearsay

Hearsay is defined as an out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of the matter
asserted.2 Hearsay is not admissible except as provided by rules or statute? Exhibits 2-33 all
contain hearsay, if not hearsay on hearsay. These exhibits offer statements by unknown declarants,
or if known, declarants that have not testified or offered these exhibits. Additionally, many of the
exhibits, Exhibits 2-32, state they were recorded by an individual, James H. Word, in the years
ranging from 1972 through 1978. Mr. Mathews provided the testimony, not James H. Word.
Furthermore, there is nothing in Mr. Mathews’ testimony to indicate that Mr. Word was the one
who obtained the information and documented it in these exhibits. Regardless, even if it is James
H. Word who had the information and wrote it down, the documents (Exhibits 2-32) are all riddled
and full of inadmissible hearsay, and all should be stricken from Mr. Mathews’ direct testimony.

Furthermore, Mr. Mathews' testimony provided no evidence and no facts that show an

exception to the rule against hearsay should apply as permitted under Tex. R. Evid. 803.

D. Lack of Authentication for Exhibits 2- 33 Tex. R. Evid. 901 and 902

Evidence must be properly authenticated before it is admitted. A witness offering evidence,

such as exhibits, must satisfy this requirement by authenticating and identifying the item of

evidence. The witness “must produce evidence sufficient to support a finding that the item is what

the proponent claims it is.” * Mr. Mathews has failed to satisfy this requirement for Exhibits 2-33;

he does not provide any evidence that any of these exhibits are what they purport to be. Mr.

Mathews does not produce any evidence or offer any testimony that these exhibits are true and

accurate or that they have not been altered in any way, nor does he offer what facts or data they

summarize. He does not present any testimony on who prepared them and when, or if they were

prepared based on that unknown person's (or group of people's) own observation and knowledge.

Furthermore, there is nothing in his testimony to show that Exhibits 2-33 are self-authenticating

as allowed under Tex R. Evid. 902.
